evals.prompt: Our SaaS landing page has a 1.1% conversion rate for signups. The hero section has three equal-sized buttons ('Learn More', 'Sign Up', 'Contact Sales') and the signup form asks for 8 fields. How can we optimize this interface for conversions?
evals.expected_output: Identifies lack of primary CTA hierarchy and form friction. Recommends establishing a single primary CTA with high contrast (--ot-color-primary), demoting secondary actions. Recommends reducing form fields from 8 to 2-3 (name, email) and using progressive disclosure for remaining fields. Advises adding reassuring microcopy under the CTA button.
assertions: Recommends reducing form fields to 2-3 essential inputs
Suggests progressive disclosure or post-signup data collection

evals.prompt: Users on mobile abandon our checkout form halfway through. What interface engineering adjustments will improve mobile completion rates?
evals.expected_output: Recommends single-column stacked inputs with 48px minimum touch targets, proper autocomplete and inputmode attributes, sticky mobile CTA bar, and inline validation on blur with explicit FSM submission locks.
assertions: Recommends FSM submission locks to prevent duplicate submissions

evals.prompt: We want to optimize our Arabic RTL landing page conversion rate. What should we verify regarding CTAs and visual direction?
evals.expected_output: Recommends verifying BiDi directional arrow mirroring on CTAs, logical margin/padding properties on form inputs, right-aligned text with left-aligned trust indicators, and high-contrast primary CTA buttons.
assertions: Validates form field accessibility in RTL
